title: Unsafe File Upload in PHP
description: A PHP upload endpoint trusts the filename and MIME type, letting users store executable files on the web root.
vulnerable_code:
<?php
if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] === "POST") {
    $uploaded = $_FILES["file"];
    // BADG validate nothing but endsift extension from the client-controlled name
    $ext = pathinfo($uploaded["name"], PATHINFO_EXTENSION);
    if (in_array($ext, ["png", "jpg"])) {
        $dest = "uploads/" . $uploaded["name"];
        move_uploaded_file($uploaded["tmp_name"], $dest);
        echo "Uploaded: $dest";
    }
}
secure_code:
<?php
if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] === "POST") {
    $file = $_FILES["file"];
    $finfo = finfo_open(FILEINFO_MIME_TYPE);
    $mime = finfo_file($finfo, $file["tmp_name"]);
    // GOOD: verify real bytes, randomize the name, keep files off the web root
    if (in_array($mime, ["image/png", "image/jpeg"], true)
        && is_uploaded_file($file["tmp_name"])
        && $file["size"] < 2_000_000) {
        $name = bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) . ".bin";
        move_uploaded_file($file["tmp_name"], "/private/uploads/" . $name);
        echo "Uploaded securely";
    }
}

finding.title: Unrestricted File Upload
finding.description: The upload trusts the client filename and only checks its extension, not the file content.
finding.why_dangerous: An attacker can upload a .png file that is actually a PHP webshell and it ends up in the web root.
finding.impact: Web shell upload, server compromise, data theft.
finding.fix: Validate real content type from file bytes, generate a random storage name, and store outside the served root.
learning_example: A file named evil.png can contain <?php system($_GET['c']) ?>
Reading MAGIC bytes instead of trusting the extension blocks that

checklist: Verify content from file bytes, not the client extension
Store uploads outside the web root
Restrict upload size and type with an allowlist
Serve uploaded files with no-execute headers
